title: Stock market today: Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 clobbered as October closes with brutal sell-off
summary:
The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) tumbled 2.8% as a tech-fueled sell-off intensified.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) fell 1.2%, or over 650 points, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC) dropped 2%.
For the month, the Dow gained 1.5%, while the Nasdaq and S&P 500 gave up gains, falling 5.2% and 1.2%, respectively.
October marked the worst month for the Nasdaq since March 2025.
Amazon shares fell 2%, while Alphabet continued to erase market value after its stock suffered its worst day in over 20 years.

title: French economy ‘headed straight for a wall’ – finance minister
summary:
Shrinking output and accelerating inflation have added to Paris’ mounting financial troubles, official figures showFrance is “headed straight for a wall” unless it reins in its budget deficit, Finance Minister Roland Lescure has warned, as the country’s economy contracts and inflation accelerates.
Annual inflation climbed to 3.4% in October from 3.1% in September, its highest level since January 2024.
Lescure also described the economy as being “at a standstill,” underscoring the mounting financial challenges facing President Emmanuel Macron’s government.

title: Lighting design a “strategic economic investment” says Signify’s Sameer Sodhi
summary:

A building’s lighting design is one of the most influential factors but is often overlooked and seen as a “finishing touch”.
